Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme. Fix a <MATH_0002>-morphism
<MATH_0003>
of stacks in groupoids over <MATH_0004>.
Assume <MATH_0005> is representable by algebraic spaces, flat, and locally
of finite presentation. Then <MATH_0006>
is a stack in groupoids and the inclusion functor
<MATH_0007>
is representable and an open immersion.

Let <MATH_0001> be an object of <MATH_0002>. It follows
from the remark following
(<REF_0001>)
that the pullback of <MATH_0003> by <MATH_0004> belongs to
<MATH_0005> if and only if the base
change of <MATH_0006> is unramified and a local complete intersection morphism.
Note that <MATH_0007> is finite locally free (hence flat, locally of
finite presentation and universally closed) and that <MATH_0008> is
flat and locally of finite presentation by our assumption on <MATH_0009>. Then
More on Morphisms of Spaces, Lemmas
<REF_0002> and
<REF_0003>
imply exists an open subscheme <MATH_0010> such that a morphism
<MATH_0011> factors through <MATH_0012> if and only if the base change of
<MATH_0013> via <MATH_0014> is unramified and a local complete intersection
morphism. This implies that
<MATH_0015>
is representable by <MATH_0016>. Hence the final statement of the lemma
holds. The first statement (that
<MATH_0017> is a stack in groupoids)
follows from this and
Algebraic Stacks,
Lemma <REF_0004>.
